MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  DECEMBER 12, 2017

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at
7:02 p.m. in the City Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Captain Dan Beringer, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, Lomita Station led those present
in the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman.

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Administrative Serviced Director Mike Whitehead
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT “RECYCLING HERO” DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR’S FREE
  RESIDENTIAL REFUSE SERVICE.

  WINNING ENTRY WAS 50 MISTY ACRES ROAD, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA

B.  PRESENTATION TO OUTGOING MAYOR FRANK V. ZERUNYAN

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF recognized MAYOR ZERUNYAN for his dedicated service to the
  City of Rolling Hills Estates and for the many accomplishments during his 2017 term
  as Mayor. She also thanked MAYOR ZERUNYAN for his many years of service on the
  CITY COUNCIL and presented him with a commemorative gavel and bow tie in
  recognition of his term as Mayor.

  On behalf of SENATOR BEN ALLEN, Olina Wibroe presented a certificate of
  commendation to MAYOR ZERUNYAN to commemorate his term as Mayor and thanked
  him for his service to the community.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
DECEMBER 12, 2017
   On behalf of ASSEMBLY MEMBER AL MURATSUCHI, Andrew DeBlock presented a
  certificate of commendation to MAYOR ZERUNYAN. Mr. DeBlock also expressed his
  personal appreciation to MAYOR ZERUNYAN for his role in shaping his career as one of
  his professors during his Masters studies at USC.

  On behalf of SUPERVISOR JANICE HAHN, Mark Waronek presented a certificate of
  commendation to MAYOR ZERUNYAN in recognition of his service to the community.

  Mr. Waronek, City of Lomita Councilmember also presented MAYOR ZERUNYAN with a
  certificate of recognition on behalf of the California Contract Cities Association and
  thanked MAYOR ZERUNYAN for his service to the City of Rolling Hills Estates, the
  regional community and the State of California.

  Captain Dan Beringer, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department presented a certificate
  of appreciation to MAYOR ZERUNYAN on behalf of SHERIFF JIM McDONNELL in
  recognition of his service to the community.

  On behalf of the Consulate General from the Republic of Armenia in Los Angeles,
  MAYOR HUFF presented a certificate of recognition to MAYOR ZERUNYAN in recognition
  of his valuable contribution to the Armenian-American community.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted his appreciation for the kind words expressed this evening
  and thanked the other local elected officials, as well as their staff, for the certificates
  and for taking the time to come this evening. He commented that it is a privilege to
  serve with them.

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 28, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 28, 2017.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – NOVEMBER AND DECEMBER 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 59282 THROUGH 59309 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $480,948.20; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 110117 THROUGH 110817;
  59141 THROUGH 59153; 59203 THROUGH 59228; AND 59627 THROUGH
  59281 IN THE AMOUNT OF $319,835.46 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF
  $800,783.66 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz Zerunyan and Zuckerman.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
DECEMBER 12, 2017
 6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
  consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
  cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered
  under New Business.)

  COUNCILMEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A-C.

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the City
  Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by title only.

  APPROVED.

B.  SEMI-ANNUAL CODE ENFORCEMENT REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

C.  FIVE YEAR UPDATE REPORT ON THE CITY’S DEVELOPMENT IMPACT FEE PROGRAM

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

7.  COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

  OUTGOING MAYOR ZERUNYAN thanked the current and past COUNCIL MEMBERS for
  their support. He commented that they are amazing public servants and he has enjoyed
  serving with them. He noted the importance of City Council’s being able to work together
  and to speak as “one voice.” He further expressed his appreciation for the congenial
  relationship he shares with his colleagues as well as his appreciation for staff.

  OUTGOING MAYOR ZERUNYAN further noted his appreciation of his role as an elected
  official and reflected on his feelings of being an American because he has been given so
  much in contrast to everything that was taken away from his family in Armenia. In
  providing background on his heritage and his position as a professor at USC, he stated
  that he is grateful for the opportunity to express the greatness of America and expressed
  sincere appreciation to those who serve this country. Finally, he sincerely thanked his
  family and friends for their invaluable support.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL

  TO APPOINT BRITT HUFF AS MAYOR BY ACCLAMATION.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
DECEMBER 12, 2017
   MAYOR HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN

  TO APPOINT JUDY MITCHELL AS MAYOR PRO TEM BY ACCLAMATION.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR HUFF SO ORDERED.

  MAYOR HUFF expressed her appreciation in being selected to serve as Mayor for 2018 and
  thanked the other members of the COUNCIL for their support and mentorship in her
  position on the COUNCIL. She further expressed appreciation to the members of the public
  present as well as her family for their support. She further expressed the importance of
  grassroots involvement to the democratic process. She commented that one of her
  priorities for 2018 is to address emergency preparedness community and Peninsula wide.

  ***

  At 7:51 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the meeting to a brief reception.

  MAYOR HUFF called the meeting back to order at 8:21 p.m.

  ***

8.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA/WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

  Martin Gombert, Administrator, Palos Verdes Peninsula Transit Authority, announced
  that PV Transit will offer free dial-a-ride shuttle service to and from the three Peninsula
  Cites from 6:00 p.m.-2:00 a.m. on New Year’s Eve/New Year’s Day and reservations can
  be made beginning December 21. He further noted that an advertisement will be broadcast
  on Channel 33 and brochures will be available.

9.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

  NONE

10.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  BUSINESS LICENSE ORDINANCE REVISIONS

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Review the proposed ordinance and fiscal
  analysis at the adjourned workshop; and 2) Formally consider the proposed ordinance
  and fiscal analysis at the regular Council meeting and provide direction.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material) and
  reported that at the workshop on this topic prior to this evening’s meeting, the City
  Council provided the following direction:

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE REPORT; FORM A
  SUBCOMMITTEE (HUFF & MITCHELL) TO WORK WITH THE CHAMBER OF
  COMMERCE ON OUTREACH AND REVIEW PROPOSALS FROM TWO
  CONSULTANTS TO ASSIST WITH PUBLIC OUTREACH; AND DIRECT STAFF TO
  PREPARE THE FINAL ORDINANCE FOR APPROVAL AT THE JANUARY 23, 2018
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
DECEMBER 12, 2017
 B.  CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES CLIMATE ACTION PLAN

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Approve the Land Use and Transportation,
  Waste, Greening, and Energy Generation/Storage measures for inclusion in the City’s
  Climate Action Plan as outlined; and 2) Approve Resolution No. 2410 , which adopts the
  City’s comprehensive Climate Action Plan.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material). She
  introduced Aaron Baum, South Bay Cities Council of Governments and Jeremy Klop,
  Fehr & Peers who were present to explain the process and answer any questions. Mr.
  Baum reviewed a PowerPoint presentation outlining the process used for developing the
  Climate Action Plan to reduce greenhouse gas emissions noting that this is a visioning
  document consisting of goals, measures, strategies and sub-strategies

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ regarding the generic language regarding
  sidewalks used in the Land Use Chapter, Mr. Baum explained that the ideas and
  opportunities identified are broad in nature. Mr. Klop further explained that the suite
  of strategies can be customized for Rolling Hills Estates’ specific purposes. Assistant to
  the City Manager Davis further explained that some strategies, like “Safe Routes to
  Schools” have already been implemented.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN thanked staff, the SBCCOG and Fehr & Peers for their
  efforts in creating the Climate Action Plan and expressed his appreciation for the use of
  general terms like “consider” and “evaluate”. He noted that in Rolling Hills Estates,
  given the unique terrain, bicycling is more of a recreational endeavor than a realistic
  mode of transportation.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE LAND USE AND TRANSPORTATION,
  WASTE, GREENING, AND ENERGY GENERATION/STORAGE MEASURES FOR
  INCLUSION IN THE CITY’S CLIMATE ACTION PLAN AS OUTLINED

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. 2410 ADOPTING THE
  CITY’S COMPREHENSIVE CLIMATE ACTION PLAN.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Clerk Luce read Resolution No. 2410 by title only.

C.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF DECEMBER 4, 2017

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE PLANNING COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF DECEMBER 4, 2017.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR HUFF SO ORDERED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
DECEMBER 12, 2017
 11.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  ALTERNATIVE OPTIONS FOR PENINSULA ENHANCED WATERSHED MANAGEMENT
  PROGRAM (EWMP) REGIONAL PROJECTS TO COMPLY WITH MACHADO LAKE
  NUTRIENT AND PESTICIDE/PCB TOTAL MAXIMUM DAILY LOADS

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize a budget adjustment for FY 2017-18
  for the allocation of $60,290 in General Funds for the City’s share of preliminary design
  costs for the Torrance Airport Stormwater Infiltration Regional Project.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material). He
  introduced Kathleen McGowan, McGowan and Associates, to present the options before
  the City Council for compliance with the Machado Lake Nutrient and Pesticide/PCB
  Total Maximum Daily Loads. Ms. McGowan reviewed a PowerPoint presentation
  outlining the stormwater permit timeline; key monitoring results and issues; options for
  alternative regional projects; and recommended next steps including the timeline for
  implementation of the direction.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that the City has expended a great deal of
  funds in attempting to address this matter without solving any water quality issues. He
  expressed concern for the continuing rising costs associated with this issue and
  commented that cities cannot continue to allocate more and more funds to this issue.
  He further suggested that the law needs to be changed and this subject may ultimately
  need to be taken up with the Environmental Protection Agency given that the Regional
  Water Quality Control Board and State keep pointing the finger at others. He commented
  that he would like a seat at the negotiating table on this matter.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Ms. McGowan commented that
  depending on which option is determined to be more effective, the construction costs for
  the Torrance Airport Stormwater Infiltration Regional Project could range between $40
  million and $50 million. He further commented that there is Federal legislation pending
  that could potentially limit the amount of funds local municipalities would be required
  to spend on stormwater related matters.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ regarding the line item showing grant
  funding, Ms. McGowan explained that the City of Torrance is attempting to recover its
  costs in obtain the grant for the project design.

  Discussion ensued concerning cost sharing for the project should it be deemed feasible
  and the percentages allocated to each City; and the amount of drinking water that could
  possibly be generated if the project see completion.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHEL, Ms. McGowan reviewed the timeline for the
  project and submittal of the Time Schedule Order.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZE A BUDGET ADJUSTMENT FOR FY 2017-
  18 FOR THE ALLOCATION OF $60,290 IN GENERAL FUNDS FOR THE CITY’S
  SHARE OF PRELIMINARY DESIGN COSTS FOR THE TORRANCE AIRPORT
  STORMWATER INFILTRATION REGIONAL PROJECT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
DECEMBER 12, 2017
 B.  BID RESULTS FOR 2017-18 STREET RESURFACING PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council award the Base Bid in the amount of
  $1,094,614.75 and additive Bid A in the amount of $108,677.75 to All American Asphalt
  for the 2017-18 Street Resurfacing Project in the total amount of $1,203,292.50.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to MAYOR HUFF, Assistant City Manager Grammer commented that cost
  for the fog seal coat in the Montecillo area is approximately $19,000 but that is just an
  aesthetic fix. Discussion ensued concerning the timing for the Cal Water project that
  will affect the Montecillo area.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding the use of Proposition C and
  Measure R funds for this project, Assistant City Manager Grammer commented that the
  funds are currently available and the City will continue to accrue those funds.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that there is new technology in
  development at USC that uses a polymer instead of slurry that dries immediately and
  lasts up to ten years and he will put staff in contact with the individuals involved in the
  product for future consideration in street resurfacing projects.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ

  AWARDED THE BASE BID IN THE AMOUNT OF $1,094,614.75 AND ADDITIVE
  BID A IN THE AMOUNT OF $108,677.75 TO ALL AMERICAN ASPHALT FOR THE
  2017-18 STREET RESURFACING PROJECT IN THE TOTAL AMOUNT OF
  $1,203,292.50.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

C.  PROPOSED DEMOLITION OF COMMUNITY CENTER

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Direct staff to enter into agreements with
  Fresh Air Environmental Services, Inc. to properly abate the lead paint and asbestos
  conditions found in the Rolling Hills Estates Community Center structure; and with
  J&B Clean-Up & Hauling, Inc. to demolish the structure, concrete foundation, and
  obtain a Sewer Permit to cap the structure’s sewer line at a total cost not to exceed
  $21,215.00; and 2) Approve a budget adjustment utilizing expected Quimby Funds to
  cover the additional costs for this project.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL, Planning Director Wahba stated that the City
  is expecting Quimby funds related to the additional homes built as part of the Chandler
  project and from the 627 Deep Valley Drive mixed-use project in the next fiscal-year.

  Also in response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL, Community Services Director Clark
  stated that in the interim, the idea is to create a small picnic area next to the nature
  center; but the Park and Activities Commission will review longer-term options for future

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
DECEMBER 12, 2017
   use at the site including possibly utilizing Quimby funds to redo the nature center and
  create a community room.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN suggested other options for use of the area including that the Palos
  Verdes Land Conservancy may wish to utilize the area to create a headquarters or the
  City may wish or to create an open amphitheater in the area.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested that staff review projected Quimby funds
  and report back to the CITY COUNCIL for future planning purposes. COUNCIL
  MEMBER SCHMITZ suggested adding this matter to the agenda for the Policy
  Development Session.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL DIRECT STAFF TO ENTER INTO AGREEMENTS WITH
  FRESH AIR ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES, INC. TO PROPERLY ABATE THE
  LEAD PAINT AND ASBESTOS CONDITIONS FOUND IN THE ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES COMMUNITY CENTER STRUCTURE; AND WITH J&B CLEAN-UP AND
  HAULING, INC. TO DEMOLISH THE STRUCTURE AND CONCRETE
  FOUNDATION, AND OBTAIN A SEWER PERMIT TO CAP THE STRUCTURES
  SEWER LINE AT A TOTAL COST NOT TO EXCEED $21,215.00; AND APPROVED
  A BUDGET ADJUSTMENT UTILIZING EXPECTED QUIMBY FUNDS TO COVER
  THE ADDITIONAL COST OF THE PROJECT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

D.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 19-17 – BLUEPRINCE SOFTWARE AGREEMENT FOR
  PLANNING AND CODE ENFORCEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file this report.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material) stating that
  staff is still working with BluePrince Software to finalize conditions in the agreement for
  planning and code enforcement software and intends to bring the mater back for

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.
